title: Removing a formula field answers 409 DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE ("existing data in this column will become inaccessible") although a formula stores nothing
body:
Filed by the `repo:cloud#2` seat (seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#24145, session `session_01Cbdek8SKSHxddGqTPZXdqX`) from the objectstack-ai/cloud#2925 dev report (cloud PR #3047, report `6256739687`), out-of-scope finding 2 (class a, reach: public HTTP door). ⛔ Not a claim. Measured on a local stack at cloud's framework pin `ec749fbb44b5`.

## What was measured

- `PUT /api/v1/meta/object` that removes a formula field answers **409 `DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE`**: "Field 'f1' removed — existing data in this column will become inaccessible. — re-submit with ?force=true".
- **Control:** removing a stored text field gives the same 409, where it is true.

## Why it is wrong

A formula is computed on read and stored nowhere (ADR-0079 addendum, item 9). The message states a data loss that cannot happen, and the removal needs `?force=true`. An agent or an author then learns to send `force=true`, which also silences the real warning on a stored field.

## Target

- Removing a formula (or any other unstored) field is not a destructive change: it saves without `force`.
- Removing a stored field keeps today's 409.

Dedupe words: destructive change formula field removed, virtual field data loss warning, DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE field_removed formula, force=true formula removal.
